recentItems.title: Teen charged over Merrylands mistaken identity murder, promising NRL player arrested | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
NSW Police have charged a teenager who allegedly provided drone surveillance during a mistaken-identity underworld attack in Merrylands West. The 18-year-old, Jimmy Schulz, was arrested in West Hoxton by the Raptor Squad and has been charged with murder over the death of Joshua Macdonald. Police say a second man was arrested with Mr Schulz, 19-year-old Ratu Viliame Koroitamana, is a promising rugby league player for the Cronulla Sharks.

recentItems.title: Family of UK man detained by Saudi Arabia for years demand his release | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
The family of British businessman Rami Naimi is urging the Saudi Arabian government to release him, claiming he may have been mistakenly identified during the kingdom’s crackdown on corruption. 
The son of former Saudi oil minister Ali Al-Naimi was arrested in Dubai in 2017 and again in 2022 without charges. 
Human rights lawyer Caoilfhionn Gallagher says his detention is unlawful and unfair, amounting to a breach of the rule of law.

recentItems.title: Optus outage left dozens unable to get through to Triple Zero | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Victoria's health minister has described Friday's Optus outage that left dozens of callers struggling to get through to emergency services as "incredibly disappointing and unacceptable".

"It's the third time that we've have had an outage from either Optus or Telstra in the last 12 months," Ingrid Stitt said on Saturday.

"So we will be urgently taking up those issues with both the telcos, but also the Commonwealth."

Victoria Police has conducted dozens of welfare checks after the outage led to some customers in Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania and the Northern Territory experiencing intermittent call dropouts from about 1:30pm.

recentItems.title: Philippines Defence Secretary slams China for 'disrespectful' note at Seoul forum | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Philippines Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro did not hold back when he was interrupted by the delivery of a handwritten note at the Seoul Defence Dialogue. 

The contents of the letter seemed to refer to Beijing's stance on the South China Sea and its rejection of an international court ruling that favoured the Philippines. 

Teodoro criticised China's lack of basic decency for the interruption and their disregard for international law.   

When questioned about the incident, China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said she was unaware of the incident and called on the Philippines to "stop grandstanding and stirring up trouble".

recentItems.title: Urgent regulation needed to prevent AI’s 'Chernobyl moment': UN advisor | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
AI researcher Jacob Coxon, who worked for OpenAI and Anthropic, has warned the artificial intelligence race between developers could lead to human extinction by the end of the decade. 
An AI advisor to the United Nations is calling on governments to introduce legislation to ensure responsible development of the technology. 
Professor Dame Wendy Hall warns a big catastrophe could happen if the industry is not regulated in time.
